description: AI503 Assignment 1 SLR extraction schema. Every leaf field is a {value, ev} pair where ev = {page, section, quote, bbox, block_id}. Arrays of values become arrays of {value, ev} objects. Designed so an interactive paper explorer can show source page images with highlight overlays.

ev_shape.page: int — page number (1-indexed) from XML page='N'
ev_shape.section: string — section title from XML section='...'
ev_shape.quote: string — verbatim 80-200 chars from the source XML block
ev_shape.bbox: [x0,y0,x1,y1] in PDF point space (72 DPI), top-left origin. From marker JSON. Optional if not available.
ev_shape.block_id: string — XML block id like '/page/7/Text/12'. Optional but preferred for round-trip lookup.

first_author.note: surname of first author for Harvard inline refs

contribution.note: 1-2 sentences capturing the paper's headline novelty. Source typically Abstract or Introduction.

datasets.note: every evaluation/calibration dataset, one element per dataset

data_size.note: free-form size description, e.g. '128 calibration sequences of 2048 tokens' or '10K passages'

eval_metrics.note: every metric reported: PPL, accuracy, BLEU, ASR, etc.

key_results.note: 2-4 headline numeric results in 'X on Y at Z = N' form. Source MUST point to the table or text where the number appears. Use ev.source_table if from a table.

metrics_results.note: Long-format structured table of EVERY reported numerical result in the paper. One entry per (model x method x bit_width x dataset x metric) datapoint. Captures all values from results tables, ablations, and prose. Each entry is sourced to its table/figure with page+bbox+quote.

model.note: Specific model checkpoint, e.g. 'OPT-175B', 'LLaMA-2-7B', 'Mistral-7B-Instruct'. Use canonical names.

method.note: Quantization method or baseline label, e.g. 'GPTQ', 'AWQ', 'RTN', 'FP16', 'SmoothQuant'. Use 'FP16' (or 'BF16' / 'FP32') for unquantized baselines.

bit_width.note: Normalize to N-bit form: '2-bit', '3-bit', '4-bit', '8-bit', '16-bit'. Map 'INT4'/'W4'/'4 bits per weight'/'NF4' all to '4-bit'. Use '16-bit' for FP16/BF16 baselines.

group_size.note: Quantization group size if reported, e.g. 'g128', 'g64', 'per-channel'. Null if not applicable / not reported.

dataset.note: Specific evaluation/calibration dataset name, e.g. 'WikiText-2', 'MMLU', 'AdvBench'. Use canonical names.

metric.note: Specific metric name, e.g. 'Perplexity', 'Accuracy', 'BLEU', 'Refusal rate', 'Speedup', 'Latency (ms/token)', 'Memory (GB)'. Include unit if part of metric definition.

value.note: The reported numerical value. Prefer raw float (e.g. 8.37). Use string only if the paper reports a range or non-numeric value (e.g. '8.3-8.5').

baseline_label.note: Label of the comparison baseline if the paper reports one alongside this value, e.g. 'FP16', 'RTN'. Null if no baseline reported.

baseline_value.note: Numerical value of the baseline. Null if not applicable.

delta.note: Difference from baseline: value - baseline_value (for 'lower is better' metrics like PPL, the delta is positive when worse). Null if no baseline.

delta_unit.note: How the delta should be interpreted: 'absolute' (raw difference), 'percent' (e.g. +3% accuracy drop), 'relative' (ratio), 'x_factor' (e.g. 3.25x speedup).

headline.note: True if this value appears in the paper's abstract or introduction as a headline result. Roughly 3-5 entries per paper should be marked headline=true.

source_kind.note: REQUIRED. 'measured' = the paper itself ran the experiment to produce this number (the paper's own contribution). 'cited' = the paper reproduces a number from prior work (typically appears in a comparison table where the paper says 'baselines from [X]', or where the value is on a model the paper does not run end-to-end). When in doubt, look at table captions for phrases like 'numbers from', 'as reported in', 'reproduced from'. Stock baselines like FP32 ImageNet ResNet-18 = 69.76% are 'cited' unless the paper explicitly retrained the baseline. Numbers the paper produced by running their own code on someone else's algorithm (e.g., 'we re-ran AdaRound') ARE 'measured', not 'cited'.

metrics_results.ev_shape: Same as standard ev: {page, section, quote, bbox, block_id, source_table}. The quote MUST contain the numeric value verbatim.

bit_widths_tested.note: [2, 3, 4, 8] etc. Empty array if not a quantization paper.

speedup_claim.note: ev should point to the table/figure with the speedup number

strengths.note: 2-4 bullet strengths, each <= 25 words. Source the claim from results/abstract/conclusion.

weaknesses.note: 2-4 weaknesses the paper itself acknowledges. Source from limitations/discussion.

limitations.note: what the method does NOT do (extrapolated from scope/results). Source the bounding statement.

reports_energy_consumption.note: Watts, joules, kWh — anything past throughput.

reports_statistical_significance.note: CIs, error bars, multiple seeds, p-values.

tests_on_edge_hardware.note: Mobile / Jetson / Raspberry Pi / non-data-center GPU.

reports_real_latency_not_just_throughput.note: Per-token latency measured, not just tokens/sec.

gap_signals.note: Each boolean traced with ev showing where the evidence is (or 'no mention' if absent — use ev with section='absence' and quote=''). Aggregating these across 50 papers builds the gap matrix.

title.value: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers

contribution.value: GPTQ is a one-shot weight-only PTQ method using approximate second-order information that quantizes 175B models to 3-4 bits in ~4 GPU-hours.

ev.quote: we propose GPTQ, a new one-shot weight quantization method based on approximate second-order information
We use WikiText-2 for perplexity evaluation

key_results.value: OPT-175B at 4-bit reaches WikiText-2 PPL 8.37 vs FP16 8.34 (Δ 0.03)
3.25× decoding speedup on A100 over FP16
